LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.infoDensity: For input distribution p and channel W, write J(x,y) = p(x)W(y|x) and Q(x,y) = p(x)Pr[Y=y]. At a pair of positive joint mass, the information density in nats is i(x;y) = ln(J(x,y)/Q(x,y)). At a pair of zero joint mass its defined value is zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.support_channelJo: Every pair of positive mass under the input–output joint law also has positive mass under the independent product of the input and output marginals.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sum_mul_infoDensi: For finite alphabets, mutual information is the joint-law mean of information density, I(X;Y) = ∑ₓ ∑ᵧ Pr[X=x,Y=y] i(x;y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.infoDensityThresh: The acceptance event at threshold t contains precisely the pairs whose joint mass exceeds eᵗ times their mass under the independent product of the marginals. A zero-joint-mass pair always fails this strict test.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mem_infoDensityTh: At a pair of positive joint mass, the threshold test accepts exactly when its information density is strictly greater than t.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelJoint_info: Under the actual input–output joint law, the probability of failing the strict threshold test equals Pr[i(X;Y) ≤ t], including ties.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.indepProd_infoDen: For finite alphabets and any real t, if X and Y are sampled independently from the channel input and output marginals, the probability of passing the strict mass-ratio test is at most exp(−t).
